_comment: An Age where curtains of light stand over the cold ground (aurora-plan.md).
The word rather than the page: `aurora` is the aspect's own aiming page, minted by
`Vocabulary.aimingPages`, and an aspect already is its page -- so `art/word/aurora.json` is a
collision the vocabulary refuses outright. This is what asks for one without aiming at it.
It *means* the phenomenon outright rather than searching for one (design 8.1), which is also what
`VocabularyCheck` insists on: a preset no word can ask for arrives only by chance. The aurora is the
one thing this word means, so it arrives with its answer in hand where a tag query -- 'the bright
colourful phenomenon' -- would also have found whatever else was bright.
**It says one thing and touches one aspect, deliberately.** A narrowing word is priced in its
lowest-ordinal aspect (`Resolver.pricedIn`), and phenomena are last, so any other parameter this set
-- a climate nudge, a pool of aurora dials -- would quietly reprice this as a word about that other
thing instead. It drafted with both and they had to go (2026-08-29).
Neither is a loss. A writer who wants a cold Age has `frozen`, and `frozen auroral Age` says what it
means where one word smuggling in a temperature never did. The variation the pool was for is drawn
from the Age's seed instead, which is where the bearing already came from -- and an aurora nobody
described should differ between Ages without a writer having to buy the difference.
